stem: The UK is a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council.
explanation: The UK is one of five permanent members of the UN Security Council, which works to keep international peace and security.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: What is the Commonwealth?

options.label: An association of countries, most once part of the British Empire
A group of European countries that trade freely
A military alliance of North Atlantic countries
The parliament of the four UK countries

explanation: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of countries. Most were once part of the British Empire, and the monarch is its head.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: What is NATO?

options.label: A group of countries that agree to defend each other
A group of countries that share one currency
A court that settles trade disputes

explanation: The UK is a member of NATO, a group of European and North American countries that have agreed to help each other if they are attacked.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Which organisation created the European Convention on Human Rights?
explanation: The Council of Europe created the European Convention on Human Rights. It is separate from the European Union.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Who is the ceremonial head of the Commonwealth?
explanation: The Monarch is the ceremonial head of the Commonwealth. Most member countries were once ruled by Britain but are now independent.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: How often are the Commonwealth Games held?
explanation: The Commonwealth Games take place every four years. Athletes from all member countries come together to compete in various sports.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: How many member countries are there in the United Nations Security Council in total?
explanation: The Security Council has 15 members. There are five permanent members and ten other members who are elected for two-year terms.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Which TWO of these are values that all Commonwealth member countries agree to follow?
explanation: The Commonwealth is based on shared values like democracy and the rule of law. It also works to support human rights and development.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: In which city is the European Court of Human Rights located?
explanation: The European Court of Human Rights is in Strasbourg, France. It was set up to make sure countries follow the Human Rights Convention.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Joining the Commonwealth is a voluntary choice for a country.
explanation: Membership of the Commonwealth is voluntary. Countries choose to join to work together on common goals and values.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: In the United Nations General Assembly, how many votes does each country have?
explanation: In the General Assembly, every member country has one vote. This assembly is where all UN members can discuss global issues.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Which TWO of these international groups is the UK a member of?
explanation: The UK is part of the G7 and G20. These groups involve the world's largest economies discussing money and security matters.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: What was the European Union (EU) called when it was first created?
explanation: The EU began as the European Economic Community (EEC). It was originally formed by six countries to help trade after World War II.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: The Council of Europe has the power to make laws that all member countries must follow.
explanation: The Council of Europe cannot make laws. Instead, it creates agreements for countries to follow regarding human rights and democracy.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: What is the main purpose of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)?
explanation: The OECD aims to improve the economy and social well-being of people around the world. The UK was a founding member in 1961.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: What is the main rule of NATO regarding a member country being attacked?

options.label: Members can choose to help or not
An attack on one is an attack on all
The UN must give permission to help

explanation: NATO is built on the idea of collective defence. This means if one member is attacked, all other members will help defend them.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Which TWO of these are agencies that are part of the United Nations?
explanation: UNICEF (for children) and WHO (for health) are both UN agencies. The UN has many departments that work on specific global problems.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Who is the official that leads the work of the Commonwealth?
explanation: The Commonwealth Secretariat is led by the Secretary-General. They help manage the meetings and work of the whole organisation.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: The UK is a member of the G7. What is the main purpose of this group?

options.label: To discuss global issues like the economy
To create laws for all member states
To select the leader of the United Nations

explanation: The G7 is a group of countries with large, developed economies. The leaders of these countries meet every year to talk about important issues like the environment and security.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: Where is the International Court of Justice located?
explanation: The International Court of Justice is one of the main parts of the United Nations. It is based in the city of The Hague.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions

stem: The United Nations (UN) was set up after the Second World War to help keep world peace.
explanation: The UN was created in 1945 to help countries solve problems by talking rather than fighting. It also works to protect human rights across the world.
handbook_ref: Chapter 5 · The UK and international institutions
